population: Finnish men (Helsinki Birth Cohort Study + Helsinki Businessmen Study; 198 combined)
conclusion: T allele over-represented among men who died at an earlier age; combined OR 3.58 (95% CI 0.96-13.4) for the shorter-lived group. Authors classify the variant as an intron variant 23 bases downstream of the exon 2 boundary and note power was 28.4%.
provenance_quote: The T allele was present more often among subjects in the control group, i.e. those who died at an earlier age, than in the two groups of longer-living and healthy subjects combined.

population: Iranian elderly (Birjand Longitudinal Aging Study; 227 adults aged 60-90)
conclusion: No significant association with frailty (adjusted OR 0.96, p = 0.98). T allele frequency declined across age strata and was absent in the 80-90 group; reported as a non-significant trend. No mortality data were available.
provenance_quote: a non-significant trend was observed, suggesting a potential inverse relationship between the T allele and advanced age
